    <h1>Symmetries of the \(\sigma\) model</h1>
    <p class="course-toc-meta">Topic: Symmetries and Noether&#x27;s theorem</p>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
**The Lagrangian of the $\sigma$ model:** $$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{L} &= \frac{1}{2} \big[ (\partial_\mu \sigma)(\partial^\mu \sigma) + (\partial_\mu \boldsymbol{\pi}) \cdot (\partial^\mu \boldsymbol{\pi}) \big]
+ i \overline{\Psi} \cancel{\partial} \Psi
+ g \overline{\Psi} (\sigma + i \boldsymbol{\tau} \cdot \boldsymbol{\pi} \gamma_5) \Psi\\
&- \frac{m^2}{2} (\sigma^2 + \boldsymbol{\pi}^2) - \frac{\lambda}{4} (\sigma^2 + \boldsymbol{\pi}^2)^2,
\end{aligned}$$ where

- $\sigma(x)$ is a scalar field,

- $\boldsymbol{\pi}(x)$ is a three-component scalar field,

- $\Psi(x)$ is a doublet of fermion fields,

- $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ are the Pauli matrices.

**Symmetry:** Prove that the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}$ has the following symmetry: $$\sigma(x) \to \sigma(x),$$ $$\boldsymbol{\pi}(x) \to \boldsymbol{\pi}(x) - \boldsymbol{\alpha} \times \boldsymbol{\pi}(x),$$ $$\Psi(x) \to \Psi(x) + i \frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}}{2} \Psi(x),$$ where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is a 3-vector of infinitesimal parameters of the transformation. Find the corresponding Noether current.

:::
